output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Thank you for keeping my bag safe and for calling the number on my lab manual. I am grateful that you made the effort to contact me rather than discard it.

I am writing about the black Jansport bag I left inside the Oshodi–Igando danfo on Friday evening, 6 November, when I came down at Ikotun. It contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, I am a first-year Biology student, and I urgently need these things for my BIO 101 practical on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m. We are not allowed into the practical without our dissecting kits, so not getting the bag back could mean missing the practical.

I appreciated how politely you spoke to me during our first call. However, the request for ₦40,000, and being told to “forget the bag” if I could not pay, left me worried. I genuinely cannot afford that amount. It is more than the value of the bag and books, and I cannot raise it.

What I can manage is ₦10,000 towards your transport and as a sincere thank-you. That is my entire allowance, and it is the most I can offer. I can give it to you when we meet and you hand over the bag. I respectfully ask that you accept this and return my belongings.

Please let me know a convenient day and time before Wednesday. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me, and we can meet during the daytime at Ikotun roundabout or outside the gate of Ikotun Police Division, whichever is easier for you. I am suggesting these simply as public, easy-to-find meeting points.

I hope we can settle this calmly and respectfully. Please reply to confirm whether you will accept the ₦10,000 and when we can collect the bag.

Thank you for your understanding.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your name]
